description: Three-panel composite figure reporting the tensile response of three austenitic low-density steels. (a) True stress (MPa, 0-2000) versus true strain (0.0-0.4) curves for four labelled specimens: 15Mn5Ni (RD) in blue, 15Mn5Ni (TD) in green, 28Mn5Ni in red and 28Mn0Ni in black. The two 15Mn5Ni curves nearly coincide, ending close to the 1500 MPa gridline by about true strain 0.15, while 28Mn5Ni and 28Mn0Ni follow almost overlapping, slowly rising curves that extend beyond true strain 0.3 and approach the same 1500 MPa level. An inset magnifies the yield region (true strain 0.005-0.020, stress ~900-1250 MPa) and shows no plateau. A boxed note gives "Tensile Test, T = 300 K, ε̇ = 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹". (b) ln σ versus ln ε (ln σ 6.4-7.6, ln ε -6 to -1) for the three RD curves, with dashed two-slope fits and slope triangles annotated n = 0.16 (15Mn5Ni) and n = 0.30 (28Mn5Ni, 28Mn0Ni). (c) Strain-hardening rate θ versus σ−σy (0-800 MPa) on a broken ordinate (0-4500 and 15000-18000 MPa): 15Mn5Ni (blue) falls steeply from above 15000 MPa to a serrated near-constant level just above the 1500 MPa gridline; 28Mn0Ni (black) declines more gently to a plateau near 2000 MPa, rises slightly, then decays toward 1500 MPa near 700 MPa. The panels together argue that stronger, less ductile 15Mn5Ni hardens less (lower n) and sheds its hardening rate much faster than the 28Mn alloys.

subfigures.description: True stress (MPa) vs true strain (0-0.4) engineering-style flow curves for four conditions: 15Mn5Ni (RD) blue, 15Mn5Ni (TD) green, 28Mn5Ni red, 28Mn0Ni black. The 15Mn5Ni curves are short and reach ~1500 MPa at low strain; the 28Mn alloys show long, nearly coincident rising curves. Inset magnifies the yield region (strain 0.005-0.020, stress ~900-1250 MPa) with no plateau. Boxed text: Tensile Test, T = 300 K, ε̇ = 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹.

Logarithmic plot ln σ vs ln ε (ln σ 6.4-7.6; ln ε -6 to -1) for the three RD flow curves. Dashed straight-line fits define two slope regimes, with slope triangles annotated n = 0.16 for 15Mn5Ni and n = 0.30 for 28Mn5Ni and 28Mn0Ni.

Strain-hardening rate θ vs σ−σy (MPa) with a broken y-axis (0-4500 and 15000-18000 MPa). 15Mn5Ni (blue) drops from above 15000 MPa steeply to a serrated plateau slightly above 1500 MPa; 28Mn0Ni (black) falls gently to a ~2000 MPa plateau, rises slightly over a long stress range, then decreases. 28Mn5Ni is absent.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a true stress (MPa, 0-2000) versus true strain (0.0-0.4) plot containing four labelled curves: 15Mn5Ni (RD) blue, 15Mn5Ni (TD) green, 28Mn5Ni red and 28Mn0Ni black.

The 15Mn5Ni (RD) and (TD) curves practically coincide and terminate near the 1500 MPa gridline at roughly true strain 0.15, whereas 28Mn5Ni and 28Mn0Ni extend beyond true strain 0.3 and end close to the same 1500 MPa level.
A boxed annotation inside panel (a) reads 'Tensile Test, T = 300 K, ε̇ = 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹'.
An inset in panel (a) magnifies the yield region over true strain 0.005-0.020 and stress ~900-1250 MPa; no plateau (flat yield region) is visible in it.
Panel (b) plots ln σ (6.4-7.6) against ln ε (-6 to -1) for the 15Mn5Ni, 28Mn5Ni and 28Mn0Ni RD curves, with dashed straight-line fits drawn over two strain ranges.
Slope triangles in panel (b) are annotated n = 0.16 for 15Mn5Ni and n = 0.30 for the 28Mn0Ni/28Mn5Ni curves.
Panel (c) uses a broken ordinate axis with segments 0-4500 and 15000-18000 MPa for the strain-hardening rate θ, and an abscissa σ−σy from 0 to 800 MPa.

In panel (c) the 15Mn5Ni curve falls almost vertically from above 15000 MPa to a near-constant, strongly serrated level just above the 1500 MPa gridline, while the black 28Mn0Ni curve decreases gently to a plateau near 2000 MPa, then rises slightly before declining toward 1500 MPa near σ−σy ≈ 700 MPa.

The caption identifies panel (b) as a logarithmic plot of the true stress-true strain curves of the three alloys and states that panel (c) shows strain hardening rate-stress curves only for 28Mn0Ni and 15Mn5Ni.

The citing text states that the 15Mn5Ni alloy exhibited significantly higher yield and tensile strengths and reduced ductility than the other two LDS alloys, while differences between 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni were minor.

The citing text states that the strain hardening exponent n at higher tensile strains is ~0.30 for 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni versus ~0.16 for 15Mn5Ni, and that the n value at low strains is small and independent of alloy composition.
The citing text states that the flow curves along RD and TD of 15Mn5Ni were almost similar with no noticeable plateaus, indicating minimal tensile anisotropy after hot-rolling.
The citing text states that the strain hardening behaviour of 28Mn5Ni is similar to that of 28Mn0Ni and therefore is not plotted in panel (c).
